plan.description: Exercise the actual pipelineDecode with completed successful and failed interface futures, recording Response access ordering and the resulting follower match index.

harness.description: A buffered Consumer channel supplies one already-completed future per independent case. The actual decoder runs with initialized follower and commitment state. The future records whether Error returned before Response access. Response closes a dedicated stop channel; this affects only the next decoder iteration, allowing the current iteration's progress effects to complete. finishCh synchronizes final state inspection. The timeout is an execution bound, not evidence of ordering. No network schedule control is claimed.
semantic_changes: Replace the pipeline and future with controlled implementations of the supplied interfaces; retain the actual pipelineDecode, updateLastAppended, and commitment code.
Supply immutable completed error status and explicitly controlled response fields. Success=true on a failed future is an artificial input, not an observed built-in transport response.
Instrument Response access and stop the decoder after the exercised iteration through its existing stop channel.
Initialize isolated replication state directly instead of starting a cluster. Observe the real commitment match map after decoder completion.
Disable legacy telemetry duplication; no protocol decision is changed.

legality.derivation: AppendPipeline.Consumer exposes ready futures without a success-only restriction. The network implementation also delivers futures after responding with their error status. AppendFuture.Response explicitly requires a preceding Error return and permits response validity only on success. Controlled completed futures therefore exercise the accepted local interface boundary. The request contains one current-term entry for a configured voter; only the actual decoder can submit its index to the initialized commitment object.
legality.applicability: Local interface consumption and its immediate replication progress effect. This setup establishes neither built-in transport production of the artificial failed response nor a legal cluster history producing incorrect commitment.
unresolved: Built-in producer reachability of a failed future with response fields that pass the decoder guards remains unresolved.
The interface substitute does not reproduce network decoding, shutdown, or peer replacement.
alternatives: Network delivery orders internal completion before Consumer delivery, but that ordering does not itself constitute an Error method return or establish successful completion.
Success=false can prevent a progress report even if the response-access precondition is violated.

grounding.derivation: The instrumented future records actual Response entry and whether the decoder previously completed its synchronous Error call. The independent requirement is the explicit AppendFuture.Response precondition.
grounding.applicability: Every observed Response access on a delivered controlled future, including the successful control.
unresolved: Availability from internal completion is distinct from compliance with the explicit Error-call contract.

grounding.derivation: A failed future has no contractually valid response. In this isolated single-delivery execution, a change to the follower's actual match index witnesses progress submitted through updateLastAppended. Compare the resulting index with the independently recorded pre-delivery index.
grounding.applicability: Completed failed-future cases only; the successful case provides a control observation.
unresolved: A measured change establishes only local consumption of the controlled failed response, not built-in transport reachability or incorrect cluster commitment.
alternatives: A failed response whose Success field is false may leave the match index unchanged despite an invalid Response access.

observable_properties.description: For each delivered future, any observed Response access must follow a completed Error call on that same future.
For each failed completed future selected by the monitor, the follower match index after decoder completion must equal its correlated pre-delivery value.

uncertainties: Artificial failed-future response contents are controlled interface inputs; they are not evidence of a built-in producer emitting those fields.
The match-map comparison detects an effective progress update in this initialized state, not every possible invocation of commitment.match.
The Error marker is set immediately before its synchronous return; the controlled Error implementation has no blocking or intervening calls, and the decoder invokes the methods sequentially.
No observation here establishes incorrect commitment, application, client completion, or deployment activation.
Missing result events, timeout, panic, and compilation errors are execution outcomes, not completed property comparisons.
